title: AMS filament loading error
shortDescription: AMS could not feed filament to the extruder.
fullDescription:
Error 12101 appears when the AMS is told to load filament but the extruder does not detect it arriving. Common reasons are a filament tip that jammed in the PTFE hub, a tangled spool inside the AMS, or a worn feeding gear.

Studio/Handy prompts to retry or give up. Always clear the filament path before retrying — blindly retrying grinds the gear.

causes.cause: Filament tangled on spool in AMS
PTFE hub clogged with filament snippets

fixSteps.title: Unload all filament
fixSteps.instruction: Unload each AMS slot and check for tangles or stuck tips.

fixSteps.title: Clear PTFE hub
fixSteps.instruction: Open the AMS back cover and remove any snapped filament from the central hub.

fixSteps.title: Reload with clean-cut tips
fixSteps.instruction: Cut each filament to a 45° clean tip before reloading.

whenToCallPro: If the AMS motor itself has failed.

faq.q: Can I skip a failed slot?
faq.a: Yes — disable the slot in Studio and continue with remaining spools.

title: AMS filament unload error
shortDescription: AMS could not retract filament back into the unit.
fullDescription:
Error 12102 fires when the AMS tries to unload filament but the sensor never sees it leave the extruder. Usually a filament break inside the Bowden tube or a blob that got stuck in the cutter area is the cause.

Manually retract the filament and inspect the Bowden tube and extruder.

fixSteps.title: Manually push filament out
fixSteps.instruction: From the AMS end, push the filament through by hand to clear the Bowden.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cutter area
fixSteps.instruction: Open the toolhead cover and remove filament debris from cutter.

whenToCallPro: If the toolhead cutter is bent.

faq.a: No — multi-color prints abort until resolved.

title: Nozzle partial or full clog
shortDescription: Printer detected abnormal extrusion — nozzle likely clogged.
fullDescription:
The X1C uses force sensors to detect abnormal extrusion. When back-pressure is excessive, it flags a clog and pauses. P1S/P1P lack the sensor but show the same symptoms (under-extrusion, skipped steps).

A cold pull with the Bambu cleaning kit resolves most clogs.

causes.cause: Heat creep from failing hotend fan

fixSteps.title: Cold pull
fixSteps.instruction: Use the cleaning kit: heat to 240°C, push white cleaning filament, cool, pull.

fixSteps.title: Check hotend fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the hotend cooling fan is running at power-on.

fixSteps.title: Replace nozzle/hotend
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the complete hotend assembly (Bambu quick-swap).

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed — Bambu hotend is user-serviceable.
videoSearchQuery: Bambu Lab X1 nozzle clog fix

faq.q: Can I clean a clogged nozzle?
faq.a: Yes via cold pulls — but replacement is often faster.

title: Chamber temperature exceeded limit
shortDescription: Printer enclosure temperature too high for current filament.
fullDescription:
X1C and X1E monitor chamber temperature. Printing PLA in a fully closed enclosure can trigger this because PLA softens at 60°C. The printer pauses to protect the print.

Open the glass door and lid, or remove top cover when printing PLA.

fixSteps.title: Open door and top
fixSteps.instruction: Open glass door and remove top cover when printing PLA.

fixSteps.title: Check auxiliary fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the aux part fan runs and is not blocked.

faq.q: Can I print ABS with door open?
faq.a: No — ABS needs a closed chamber.

title: Printer lost cloud or LAN communication
shortDescription: Bambu Studio lost contact with the printer during a print.
fullDescription:
Losing communication does not stop the print — the printer continues from its own storage. But you cannot monitor it from Studio or Handy until the link returns.

Usually this is a Wi-Fi router dropout, a Bambu cloud outage, or the printer being on 5GHz with a weak signal.

fixSteps.title: Check Wi-Fi signal
fixSteps.instruction: Move router closer or add a repeater if the signal is poor at the printer.

fixSteps.title: Switch to LAN mode
fixSteps.instruction: In printer settings enable LAN-only mode for local control if cloud is flaky.

videoSearchQuery: Bambu Lab lost connection during print

faq.q: Will the print fail if comm drops?

title: Wi-Fi connection unstable
shortDescription: Printer frequently drops and reconnects to Wi-Fi.
fullDescription:
Bambu printers support 2.4GHz only. If you're connecting to a mesh network that prefers 5GHz, the printer can roam between nodes and drop often.

Creating a dedicated 2.4GHz SSID or locking to a specific band fixes most cases.

fixSteps.title: Create dedicated 2.4GHz SSID
fixSteps.instruction: In router settings, separate 2.4GHz into its own SSID and connect printer there.

title: Build plate mismatch or not detected
shortDescription: Printer detected a different plate than the sliced profile expects.
fullDescription:
Each Bambu plate has an RFID tag. If the tag is unreadable or a third-party plate is used, the printer warns. You can continue manually but plate-specific temperatures will not auto-adjust.

Clean the plate backside and ensure it's fully seated on the heatbed.

fixSteps.title: Clean plate underside
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the plate backside with IPA to clear the RFID area.

fixSteps.title: Select plate manually
fixSteps.instruction: In Studio, manually set build plate type to match your third-party plate.

videoSearchQuery: Bambu Lab build plate not detected

title: Filament tangled inside AMS
shortDescription: Filament in the AMS is tangled and cannot be pulled.
fullDescription:
Tangling usually happens when a spool is loaded without tension and the end slips under another turn. The AMS motor cannot pull and triggers a feed error.

Always ensure the filament end is secured in the spool's hole before loading.

causes.cause: Filament end slipped under another loop

fixSteps.title: Open AMS
fixSteps.instruction: Open the AMS lid and pull out the affected spool.

fixSteps.title: Unwind tangle
fixSteps.instruction: Carefully unwind the crossed loops and rewind onto the spool.

faq.a: Always secure the filament end before removing a spool.

title: Print layers shifted
shortDescription: Layers offset — X/Y axis skipped steps.
fullDescription:
Bambu CoreXY printers can still shift if belts are loose or the toolhead has debris stuck in the motion path. High-speed printing is aggressive on belts — check tension every few months.

Run the auto belt tension check in the printer menu.

fixSteps.title: Auto belt tension
fixSteps.instruction: Run the built-in belt tension test from the printer's menu.

fixSteps.title: Clean rails
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe linear rails with a lint-free cloth and apply a drop of rail oil.

whenToCallPro: If belts need replacement and you are not comfortable with CoreXY routing.

faq.q: How often should I check belts?

title: Built-in camera offline
shortDescription: Internal camera feed is unavailable in Studio or Handy.
fullDescription: The internal camera streams over the cloud or LAN. Issues stem from insufficient Wi-Fi bandwidth, a bent ribbon cable to the camera module, or a firmware bug. Reboot first, then try LAN-only mode.

fixSteps.title: Reseat camera ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Open the top cover and reseat the FFC on the camera PCB.

whenToCallPro: If the camera module itself has failed.

faq.q: Is the camera critical for printing?

title: Stepper motor fault
shortDescription: Motor driver reports a fault — typically overcurrent or overtemperature.
fullDescription:
Bambu uses TMC drivers with fault reporting. A motor fault usually means the driver overheated (blocked fan) or the motor phase wiring shorted. The axis stops immediately.

Inspect the motor connector for damage before rebooting.

fixSteps.title: Inspect motor connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check motor plug for loose pins or melted plastic.

whenToCallPro: If driver chip on mainboard is damaged.

faq.q: Will a motor fault damage other parts?

title: First layer not sticking to plate
shortDescription: Print lifts or does not stick during first layer.
fullDescription:
Poor adhesion is caused by oily fingerprints on the plate, wrong plate type selected, or Z-offset too high. Bambu's textured PEI is excellent for PLA/PETG but needs glue stick for PA/TPU.

Clean with dish soap and hot water, rinse, and dry.

fixSteps.title: Wash plate
fixSteps.instruction: Remove plate, wash with dish soap and hot water, dry fully.

fixSteps.title: Adjust Z offset
fixSteps.instruction: Use Studio live-Z to bring nozzle 0.02mm closer if needed.

fixSteps.title: Apply glue for tough filaments
fixSteps.instruction: Thin layer of glue stick for PA, TPU, and ABS.
